metadata.title: Open-source Next.js SaaS starter
metadata.description: An open-source Next.js SaaS starter with guided setup, authentication, organizations, Stripe, credits, private storage, durable jobs, Content Studio, observability, and tested operations.

useCase.title: DojoClip: an AI media SaaS.
useCase.body: DojoClip builds video editing, image, music, and voice workflows on a SaaS foundation. See which parts the starter supplies and where the product adds its own media experience.

landing.subtitle: Go from guided local setup to a deployable web app, admin console, and Content Studio—with replay-safe billing, private storage, durable work, observability, and restore-tested operations.
landing.fitAction: See when Sushi SaaS is a good fit.

signals.title: One-command development
signals.body: Setup, doctor, unified runner, safe fixtures, and local Postgres, Redis, and Garage.

signals.title: Replay-safe money
signals.body: Idempotent checkout, webhooks, ledger spends, and exactly-once compensation.

signals.title: Deployable operations
signals.body: Portable workers, containers, readiness, telemetry, backups, retention, and launch audits.

signals.title: Tests as architecture
signals.body: Layering, auth gates, replay behavior, migrations, and DB constraints are executable.

journeys.title: Enter through the question you have now.
journeys.intro: New adopters need different levels of detail. Start the complete stack, trace one paid workflow, or inspect the production controls before choosing what to keep.

items.title: Explore the starter
items.body: Install it, customize the product identity, verify local dependencies, seed a demo account, and open every shipped application.

items.title: Learn one complete feature
items.body: Follow the five-credit image task through authentication, entitlements, ledger replay, the durable worker, private output, and compensation.

items.title: Prepare a real launch
items.body: Build hardened containers, inspect migrations and data integrity, run restore drills, and execute the launch-readiness audit.

systems.title: A backbone, not a demo.
systems.intro: The starter focuses on the parts that become expensive after launch: ownership, retries, reconciliation, operational access, and explicit boundaries.

items.title: Authentication & abuse controls
items.body: Verified email flows, OAuth, password recovery, MFA, Turnstile, Redis rate limits, and authentication event history.

items.title: Billing & entitlements
items.body: Stripe Prices drive checkout; lifecycle webhooks update organization subscriptions and capability checks.

items.title: Credit accounting
items.body: An append-only, traceable ledger connects purchases, grants, task spending, reversals, and balances.

items.title: Organizations & teams
items.body: Personal and shared workspaces, invitations, roles, last-owner protection, and pooled resources.

items.title: Storage & jobs
items.body: Private S3-compatible objects, signed access, generated outputs, lifecycle state, and a durable retryable database queue.

items.title: Operator console
items.body: A separately deployed admin application with MFA, read/write roles, job recovery, audit events, and billing visibility.

items.title: Content & lifecycle
items.body: An independently deployed Payload studio, signed marketing gateway, consent records, account exports, and delayed erasure.

items.title: Release operations
items.body: OpenTelemetry, structured logs, migration integrity, backups, restore drills, retention, containers, and launch checks.

referenceFlow.title: One image request crosses the whole SaaS backbone.
referenceFlow.intro: The local image provider is deliberately simple. The value is the production-shaped chain around it: one request key, one five-credit spend, durable execution, private output, and a refund that can recover after a crash.

steps.title: Authorize
steps.body: Resolve the member, organization, capability, quota, and same-origin boundary.

steps.title: Reserve
steps.body: Persist a fingerprinted task and a deterministic five-credit ledger spend.

steps.title: Dispatch
steps.body: Deduplicate a durable job that survives the original HTTP request.

steps.title: Generate
steps.body: Call the provider with a stable idempotency identity and bounded retries.

steps.title: Store
steps.body: Write and verify a private Garage/S3 object, then return a short-lived signed URL.

steps.title: Compensate
steps.body: On terminal failure, restore the spend exactly once before the task becomes failed.

architecture.title: One direction through the codebase.
architecture.intro: Routes translate HTTP. Services own invariants. Models own queries. The database owns constraints. Tests stop those boundaries from quietly dissolving.

steps.title: Routes
steps.body: Authenticate, validate, and translate HTTP into a business operation.

steps.title: Services
steps.body: Coordinate invariants, idempotency, authorization, and side effects.

steps.title: Models
steps.body: Provide typed, tenant-aware persistence behind one query boundary.

steps.title: Database
steps.body: Enforce uniqueness, ownership, references, and durable state transitions.

closing.title: Start closer to the part only your company can build.

docs.title: Build and operate Sushi SaaS
docs.intro: Choose a task for exact setup and verification steps. When you need to understand a choice or decide what to change, use Guides.

blogs.title: Understand and adapt Sushi SaaS
blogs.intro: See what the starter chooses, why it chooses it, which alternatives fit, and what to keep, change, or remove for your product.
blogs.empty: No guides have been published yet.

privacy.title: Privacy notice
privacy.description: How this documentation website handles visitor information.
privacy.notice: This notice covers the documentation website only. Products built from the starter need their own policy based on the services and data they use.

sections.heading: Information processed
paragraphs: This website serves public documentation. It does not create customer accounts, accept payments, or store product uploads.
The hosting provider may process routine request data such as an IP address, user agent, requested URL, and timestamp to deliver and protect the site.

sections.heading: Analytics and cookies
paragraphs: Analytics are disabled by default. If privacy-respecting analytics are enabled later, this notice and the consent experience must be updated before collection starts.
The site may use strictly necessary preferences, such as a chosen language or theme.

sections.heading: External links
paragraphs: Documentation links to GitHub and third-party provider documentation. Their privacy practices apply after you follow those links.

sections.heading: Questions
paragraphs: Open an issue in the linked source repository for questions about this notice or the documentation website.
